Now my HOD and parents expect me to maintain this, but I know I'm not a 9-pointer kid. I'm actively thinking of messing up my upcoming DSA lab exam on purpose just to bring my grades down to a 'safe' level where no one expects anything from me.

They made me the lead for our college's annual national hackathon team because of some stupid web-dev project I built last year. I should be thrilled, but my stomach is in knots. If we win or even do well, the expectations for my placements are going to skyrocket, and I'll be expected to lead everything from now on. I’m thinking of leaving the WhatsApp group and ghosting the team because being known as a failure feels so much safer than having to be 'on' all the time.

Professor Roy offered me a funded research assistantship because he liked my final year project proposal. But I didn't even write half of it myself—I used ChatGPT and got help from a senior. If I accept, I'll be working 10 hours a week in his lab under his direct supervision, and he's going to see how slow I actually am at debugging. I haven't replied to his email in four days and I'm hoping he just gives the spot to someone else so I can stop feeling this paralyzing dread of being exposed.

I actually cleared the coding round for a major tech firm today. My friends are treating me like some kind of coding god, but I'm literally shaking in the hostel bathroom. If I pass the system design round tomorrow, my life changes, the stakes get real, and I'll have to actually perform at a high level every single day. I'm so tempted to just 'forget' to log into the coding portal tomorrow morning because the comfort of being a struggling student feels infinitely safer than the terrifying weight of actual success.

Day 3 of campus placement season. I cleared the FAANG shortlists after grinding LeetCode for a year. Now my final interviews are tomorrow morning and I am literally throwing up because if I actually clear this, the expectations will be insane. I am genuinely thinking of pretending my internet died or sleeping through the alarm. If I fail now, at least I stay in my comfortable zone of being an 'underachiever with potential' instead of getting exposed as a complete fraud on a 40 LPA package.

Last semester I somehow landed a 9.6 CGPA and my face was put on the department topper board. Since then, I've been physically sick with dread. Our midterms start Monday and I haven't even opened my DSA notes or touched my laptop because if I score high again, the pressure to keep doing it will kill me. I want to fail this paper on purpose just so everyone stops expecting me to be this genius I know I'm not.

They made me the team lead for our final year capstone project because our machine learning prototype won a local hackathon. But now we have to submit the model for the national expo, and I've been secretly delaying the Git pushes and making excuses to my team. If we win this, we'll have to pitch to actual venture capitalists and I know I will choke and humiliate everyone. It feels so much safer if our project just gets disqualified due to 'technical issues' so I can go back to being invisible.

A senior from my college got me a direct referral for a high-stipend winter internship at an investment bank. All I have to do is upload my resume and do a basic coding screening, but the link expires tonight and I’m just staring at my screen. If I get in, they will realize my system design concepts are trash and I'll get blacklisted or fired in a week. If I just don't apply, I can keep pretending I had a shot instead of actually failing in public.

I got an 8 LPA on-campus offer, which is honestly decent. But my dad went ahead and called all my relatives saying 'this is just the start, he's going for 25 LPA off-campus next'. Now I have an interview shortlist for a top product company, and I'm actively wishing I fail the HR round. If I get the bigger offer, the family expectations will become a black hole I can never escape, and if I fail after getting so close, I'll be the ultimate laughingstock.

I somehow cleared the Amazon DSA round. Literally everyone is congratulating me in the hostel WhatsApp group, but my stomach is in knots. I’m actually praying I fail the system design round tomorrow. If I get this internship, everyone’s expectations will skyrocket, and when they realize I can't even write a clean DFS code without StackOverflow, the fall is going to kill me. It’s safer to just mess up tomorrow on purpose so I can stay in my lane.

I got a 9.6 CGPA this semester and honestly, I wish I got an 8. Now my parents are talking about me getting a 15 LPA package minimum, and my prof wants me to lead the department's tech fest. I feel like an imposter who accidentally guessed all the MCQs right. I’m literally sitting here thinking of skipping my DSA lab evaluation tomorrow just to bring my average down so everyone stops looking at me like I’m some kind of genius.

My IoT prototype got shortlisted for the college startup grant. I should be celebrating, but I’ve been having mini panic attacks since morning. If I accept the money, I have to hire juniors, report to the dean, and actually build a market-ready product. I’m just a tier-3 college kid who built this using YouTube tutorials; if I take this on, I know I will mess up on a bigger stage, and the humiliation will be public.

I’ve been topping the mock placement leaderboards for three weeks straight. But lately, I’ve started staying up until 4 AM playing Valorant and purposely waking up late for the actual company presentations. It's like my brain is trying to ruin my chances because the thought of actually clearing the interviews, moving to Bangalore, and managing a real software engineering job makes me want to throw up. If I stay a failure, at least I know how to handle it.

My research guide—who is notoriously brutal—emailed me saying my draft paper was 'exceptional' and that we should submit it to an IEEE journal. I haven't replied to him in four days. I’m paralyzed. If I write the next section and it's mediocre, he’ll realize the first draft was just a fluke and he’ll regret praising me. I’d honestly rather he think I’m lazy than realize I’m actually stupid.

I somehow cleared the Amazon online assessment for the SDE internship, and instead of being happy, I’m literally having a panic attack. My dad is already calling up my uncles bragging about a '40 LPA package' when I haven't even had the technical interviews yet. I feel like if I actually pass this and get the job, everyone will realize I'm a fraud who just got lucky with easy Leetcode questions, and the pressure to keep performing at that level will kill me. I’m seriously thinking about just pretending I got a fever and skipping the interview loop altogether so I don't have to face the inevitable crash.

I got a 9.6 SGPA last semester and honestly, I wish I hadn't. Now my professor keeps pointing me out in the DSA lab as 'the benchmark' for the rest of the batch, and my friends keep joking about how I'm going to save them all in the group projects. I feel this sickening weight in my chest every time I open my IDE now because if my CGPA drops even slightly, everyone will see it as this massive failure. I’ve started purposely submitting my mock tests late and leaving questions blank just to bring their expectations down to a level where I can actually breathe again.

We won first place in the college smart india hackathon last week, and now the department head wants to make me the lead coordinator for the tech fest next month. Everyone keeps saying I’m 'built for this,' but inside, I’m completely paralyzed with terror. Winning the hackathon felt like a fluke where my team did all the heavy lifting, and if I accept this leadership role, my incompetence is going to be broadcasted to the entire campus. I'm draft-saving an email to resign from the committee because if I fail as the lead, the fall from grace is going to be so much worse than if I just stay a nobody.

I finally got selected for the paid ML research project under our department’s most senior professor, which is what I’ve been crying about wanting for the last six months. But now that the offer letter is sitting in my inbox, my stomach is in knots and I can't bring myself to sign it. I keep thinking about how she expects me to write high-quality research papers, and I’m terrified that once she sees how slowly I write code and how much I struggle with math, she'll regret choosing me. I’m thinking of replying and telling her I have 'personal reasons' to decline, because declining feels like a clean break, whereas failing after accepting feels like a death sentence to my career.

I got a 5-star rating on my mock placement interview yesterday, and the training cell officer told me I’m a shoo-in for the Tier-1 companies coming next week. Instead of feeling motivated, I’ve spent the last 24 hours locked in my hostel room feeling utterly sick. If I actually get a 20+ LPA offer, it means I have to pack up, move to Bangalore, survive the corporate grind, and handle absolute independence when I can barely handle my own laundry right now. I’m literally considering skipping the placement drives and settling for some local mass recruiter because the thought of actually succeeding and having to step up to that life is making me physically vomit.

I actually cleared the round-3 coding assessment for that crazy 24 LPA tech giant, and instead of being happy, my stomach is in knots. I keep hoping they'll reject me in the final HR round because if I actually get this job, everyone will realize I just googled my way through DSA and can't code to save my life. If I fail now, it's fine, but if I succeed and then get fired for being useless, I won't survive the shame.

My professor wants to nominate me as the student lead for our department's upcoming national hackathon because of my past project. I literally want to decline it and make up some family emergency to get out of it. If I say yes, I'm signing up for a massive spotlight where every single mistake I make will be blown up, and everyone will see I'm just a mediocre coder who got lucky once.

I somehow got a perfect 10 CGPA this semester, and honestly, I wish I got an 8.5 instead. Now my parents are bragging to every relative on WhatsApp, and my professors are expecting me to lead the department research project next term. The pressure is suffocating me because I know I can't maintain this, and the drop from the top is going to hurt so much worse.

My professor nominated me for the fully-funded summer internship in Germany, and I’m genuinely thinking of rejecting it. My friends have been struggling with backlogs and bad grades, and if I take this, I know it's going to create this weird, silent wall between us. I'd rather stay back with them and be normal than be successful and completely isolated.

I'm in the final round for a huge consulting firm next week. Last night, I literally sat down and thought about intentionally bombing the case study round just to get it over with. If I actually get the offer, I'll have to move to a new city, work 80 hours a week, and prove myself all over again, and I don't think I have the stamina to keep up with who they think I am.

I somehow cleared the second round of the Amazon interview today. Instead of feeling happy, my stomach is in knots. I literally looked at the confirmation email and felt this overwhelming urge to just ghost them. If I get this job, my parents are going to tell the whole neighborhood, and then I’m stuck. Every single day will be a fight to prove I’m not a fraud who just memorized three trees-and-graphs templates on LeetCode. It feels safer to just fail the next round and blame it on hard questions so everyone stops expecting me to be some coding genius.

My professor wants to publish my DBMS project paper in an international journal and nominated me as the lead student researcher. I’ve been ignoring his emails for four days now. I keep thinking, if I say yes, I’m locking myself into this identity of a high-achiever, and I cannot keep up with that. My friends are already teasing me about getting a 'fat package' and calling me the department topper, and it makes me want to crawl into a hole. I’m seriously considering copying someone else's minor assignment just so the prof thinks I'm mediocre and leaves me alone.

I just got my 5th semester SGPA back and it's a 9.4. I should be celebrating, but honestly? I felt this cold wave of dread. The first thing I thought was, 'Now I have to maintain this.' If I drop to an 8.5 next semester, it's going to look like a massive failure compared to this, and my relatives will have a field day talking about my 'downfall.' Part of me wishes I had just got an average 7.5 so I could breathe without feeling like I'm standing on the edge of a cliff waiting to be pushed off.

Our team won the college hackathon, and they want me to present our prototype to some venture capitalists coming to campus next week. I literally told my team members to take my name off the slide and let someone else do it. Every time I think about presenting, I picture them asking deep technical questions and realizing I don't actually understand the system architecture as well as my teammates. If I do well, I’ll be expected to lead the next startup incubator phase, and I just want to hide in my room and play games. I hate that I'm sabotaging my own career, but the safety of being a nobody feels so much better than the terror of being noticed.

I got shortlisted for the final HR round of a dream product company. It pays more than double what my dad makes. But instead of studying, I spent the last two days binge-watching sitcoms and eating instant noodles. I feel this weird, heavy resistance to opening my laptop. It’s like, if I actually land this job, my whole life changes, and the expectations from my family will become unbearable—they’ll expect me to buy a house, support my cousins, and never have a weak moment. If I just mess up the HR round by giving bad answers, I can go back to being the 'struggling student' where nothing is expected of me.
